draft.title: Claiming legitimacy
card: Legitimacy means a widely accepted right to rule. Hatshepsut was a woman who took the throne, so she had to show that her rule was proper.
In her statues and reliefs she was often shown as a male king, with the kilt, crown and false beard. This fitted the traditional look of a pharaoh.
She told a story that the god Amun took the form of her father, Thutmose I, and became her real father. This presented her as chosen by the gods.
Both methods used familiar symbols of kingship. Her images showed her as a king, and the birth story gave her divine support.
draft.remember: Hatshepsut used the look of a male king and a divine birth story to show she had the right to rule.

a.q: Why did Hatshepsut have statues made that showed her wearing a king's kilt and false beard?
opts: To fit the traditional image of a pharaoh
To hide that she had ever been a regent
To show that she had been born a man
To give thanks to Amun for her victories
a.why: The kilt, crown and beard were the usual signs of a pharaoh, so wearing them presented her as a proper king. Hiding her time as regent is wrong, since the images were about her kingship and not about her past.
a.clue: Think about what a pharaoh was expected to look like.

b.q: Hatshepsut said Amun took the form of Thutmose I and became her father. What was the main purpose of this story?
opts: To present her as chosen by the gods to rule
To prove that Thutmose I had named her heir
To show that Thutmose III had no claim to rule
To explain why she had married Thutmose II
b.why: A god as her father made her rule seem approved by the gods, so it backed her right to be king. Saying Thutmose I named her heir is the most tempting wrong option, but the story is about Amun's choice, and it does not describe a decision by her human father.
b.clue: Who was her divine father said to be, and what did that suggest about the gods' view of her?

a.best: To fit the traditional image of a pharaoh

b.best: To present her as chosen by the gods to rule
